sources.entry: cAdvisor | Resource usage and performance analysis of running containers

summary.one_liner: cAdvisor is a running daemon from Google that collects, aggregates and exports resource usage and performance data for running containers.
summary.what_it_does: cAdvisor (Container Advisor) runs as a daemon and tracks resource isolation parameters, historical resource usage, histograms of historical usage, and network statistics for each container. It exports this data per container and machine-wide. It has native support for Docker containers and is described as supporting most other container types. The README describes a web UI served on its port, a versioned remote REST API with an official Go client in the client directory, and support for exporting stats to storage plugins. The README also lists a roadmap of planned performance advice, auto-tuning, and usage prediction for schedulers.
use_cases: monitor docker container cpu and memory usage
view per-container resource usage in a web dashboard
export container metrics to storage backends
run container monitoring on kubernetes as a daemonset
query container stats through a REST API
how_to_run: VERSION=0.55.1 # use the latest release version
Open the web UI at port 8080 on the host
For Kubernetes, run cAdvisor as a daemonset (see the README's linked instructions)
For versions prior to v0.53.0, use gcr.io/cadvisor/cadvisor instead of ghcr.io/google/cadvisor
notable: Native Docker container support, with a claim of support for most other container types
Built-in web UI plus a versioned remote REST API
Official Go client in the client directory
Per-container and machine-wide stats, including historical usage histograms
Container abstraction based on lmctfy, so containers nest hierarchically
caveats: Quick-start Docker run requires --privileged and several host volume mounts (/, /var/run, /sys, /var/lib/docker, /dev/disk)
README notes special running instructions for CentOS, Fedora, RHEL, and LXC
Advisory and auto-tuning features are roadmap items, not current functionality
keywords: see what my containers are using
